conditioning_event: Numerator conditions on Q47Travlooking==Yes, a single reported travel day; the cost is for that day only, not a monthly or per-trip average

units: ratio of a day-conditional transport cost to one day's wage (dimensionless)
estimator: ratio of two independently-weighted point estimates
uncertainty_method: Nonparametric bootstrap (2,000 resamples), cost and wage populations resampled independently each draw. No cluster/PSU adjustment attempted or its absence checked for NHTS specifically.

open_audit_findings: (1) The Unspecified/Not-applicable conflation in cost missingness is unresolved and could bias mean_daily_cost downward if some Unspecified respondents incurred real, unreported costs. version: published table (digitised from PDF page 39, not the R/Stata reproducibility package per D6)
hash: not applicable -- no microdata, digitised from the published PDF table
geography: 3 South African metros (Johannesburg, Cape Town, eThekwini), sub-place (admin-5) geography, standard errors clustered at main-place (admin-4) level -- confirmed against the paper's own Table 5b notes (Literature/baez_full.txt, page 40 of the PDF)
age_universe: CONFIRMED against the paper's own text (Literature/baez_full.txt lines 799-801): 'We present similar regressions using the share of working-age adults employed, drawn from the 2011 census (Table 5b).' Working-age is not itself defined to an exact age range in the extracted text (StatsSA's conventional 15-64 assumed, not independently confirmed).
labour_market_universe: CONFIRMED population-based, not labour-force-based: the paper's own text and Table 5b's title ('Spatial Correlates of Share of the Adult Population Employed') both describe the dependent variable as the share of the working-age POPULATION employed -- denominator is everyone working-age, not the labour force.
denominator: working-age adult population per sub-place, population-weighted (paper's own regression weights)
weights: sub-place-level population weights (paper's own specification); not applicable to this project beyond citing the paper's coefficient
missingness_treatment: not applicable (published coefficient, no microdata used by this project)
units: percentage points of employment share per 10 percentile points of within-city travel-time rank
estimator: OLS regression coefficient (paper's own specification; no population-density control per the notebook's own header note; robustness checked against a spatial-error specification with population density, per the paper's Table 5a/5b pairing)
uncertainty_method: Paper's own reported t-statistics; reconstructed per-city sampling SE = |coefficient|/|t-statistic| (Johannesburg 1.10, Cape Town 0.84, eThekwini 0.66), kept separate from moments.csv's standard_error, which is instead the cross-city sample SD (1.4048) used as a calibration-uncertainty scale, not a sampling SE
model_counterpart: src/moments.py distance_gradient_slope() -- OLS slope of EMPLOYED (share of the model's own agent/labour-force population) on percentile rank of distance_to_cbd
open_audit_findings: CONFIRMED MISMATCH (verified against Literature/baez_full.txt, not just the table title): the paper's dependent variable is the working-age POPULATION employment share; the model's distance_gradient_slope() is necessarily labour-force-based, since every agent is employed, searching or discouraged and there is no non-labour-force agent to include in a population denominator. E/Pop = (E/LF)*(LF/Pop), so the paper's slope conflates the model's own estimand with however labour-force participation itself varies with distance -- a channel the paper does not report and this model does not have. Recommendation (not yet decided): report the correspondence as a documented, unresolved estimand mismatch rather than treating a rescaling as available, since no participation-rate-by-distance profile exists in the cited source to correct for it. See the bounded pre-calibration specification for options.
